theme: Produce cooked as vegetables that is botanically a fruit: it develops from a flower's ovary and carries the seeds.
decoy: Garden vegetables used in savory cooking

members.title: Tomato
members.description: Juicy red globe that anchors pasta sauces, salsas, and summer salads.

members.title: Cucumber
members.description: Cool, crisp green cylinder sliced into salads or pickled with dill.

members.title: Eggplant
members.description: Glossy purple globe that turns silky when roasted, as in baba ganoush.

members.title: Bell pepper
members.description: Sweet, crunchy, blocky pod sold in green, red, yellow, and orange.

members.title: Zucchini
members.description: Long green summer squash, often grilled in planks or cut into ribbons.

members.title: Butternut squash
members.description: Tan, bell-shaped winter squash with dense orange flesh for soups.

members.title: Okra
members.description: Ridged green pods that turn silky in gumbo and Indian bhindi masala.

members.title: Avocado
members.description: Buttery, green-fleshed staple mashed into dips and spread on toast.

members.title: Green beans
members.description: Slender snap pods steamed, sauteed, or baked into a holiday casserole.

intruders.title: Artichoke
intruders.description: Green globe of tough leaves, steamed or roasted and dipped in butter.
intruders.why: The edible part is an immature flower bud, not a fruit. It is shelved and cooked alongside tomatoes and peppers.

intruders.title: Broccoli
intruders.description: Branching green stalks with dense clusters, steamed or stir-fried.
intruders.why: The edible heads are clusters of unopened flower buds on thick stems, not fruits. It is a staple vegetable like the rest.

theme: Plants of the legume (pea) family, Fabaceae.
decoy: Beans and bean-like staples

members.title: Peanut
members.description: Papery-shelled kernels roasted, salted, or ground into a smooth spread.

members.title: Chickpea
members.description: Round beige pulse mashed into hummus and fried as falafel.

members.title: Lentil
members.description: Small lens-shaped pulse simmered into dal and hearty winter soups.

members.title: Soybean
members.description: Protein-rich bean pressed for oil and turned into tofu and soy sauce.

members.title: Fava bean
members.description: Broad green bean slipped from a thick pod and then from its pale skin.

members.title: Mung bean
members.description: Small green bean sprouted for stir-fries and cooked into sweet soups.

members.title: Tamarind
members.description: Brown sticky pulp from long brittle pods, used to sour chutneys.

members.title: Carob
members.description: Dark pods milled into a sweet brown powder used much like cocoa.

members.title: Fenugreek
members.description: Bitter, maple-scented spice common in curries and Ethiopian blends.

intruders.title: Coffee bean
intruders.description: Roasted brown bean ground and brewed into the morning's dark drink.
intruders.why: The seed of a cherry-like fruit of Coffea, in the coffee family (Rubiaceae), not a legume. It is called a bean all the same.

intruders.title: Cocoa bean
intruders.description: Roasted brown bean from which chocolate and cocoa powder are made.
intruders.why: The seed of the cacao tree, in the mallow family (Malvaceae), not a legume, despite being called a bean.

intruders.title: Vanilla bean
intruders.description: Long, dark, fragrant pod split open to scrape out tiny black specks.
intruders.why: The cured seed pod of a climbing orchid, not a legume. Both its common names, bean and pod, suggest the pea family.

theme: Foods made by fermentation, in which bacteria, yeasts, or molds transform the raw ingredients.
decoy: Tangy, preserved staples of Asian and European kitchens

members.title: Kimchi
members.description: Spicy Korean napa cabbage seasoned with red pepper, garlic, and ginger.

members.title: Miso
members.description: Salty Japanese paste of soybeans and rice or barley, stirred into soup.

members.title: Tempeh
members.description: Firm Indonesian cake of whole soybeans bound into a sliceable block.

members.title: Kombucha
members.description: Tangy, fizzy sweetened tea drink, often flavored with ginger.

members.title: Kefir
members.description: Tart, drinkable dairy beverage from the Caucasus with a slight fizz.

members.title: Natto
members.description: Sticky, stringy Japanese soybeans with a pungent smell, eaten over rice.

members.title: Fish sauce
members.description: Amber, salty Southeast Asian liquid of anchovies and sea salt.

members.title: Sourdough bread
members.description: Chewy, tangy loaf with an open crumb and a thick crackling crust.

members.title: Yogurt
members.description: Thick, tangy dairy staple eaten with honey or strained for dips.

intruders.title: Tofu
intruders.description: Soft white soybean curd pressed into blocks, then braised or deep-fried.
intruders.why: Made by curdling hot soy milk with salts or acid, much like fresh cheese, with no fermentation. It sits naturally beside miso and tempeh.

intruders.title: Bread-and-butter pickles
intruders.description: Sweet, tangy sliced cucumbers and onion, sold in glass jars for burgers.
intruders.why: Packed in a vinegar-and-sugar brine: the sourness is added vinegar, not the product of fermentation like true brine pickles.

theme: Alcoholic drinks made by distillation.
decoy: Traditional alcoholic drinks from around the world

members.title: Tequila
members.description: Mexican blue-agave drink from Jalisco, sipped neat or shaken into margaritas.

members.title: Mezcal
members.description: Smoky Mexican agave drink from Oaxaca, its hearts roasted in pits.

members.title: Rum
members.description: Caribbean drink from sugarcane molasses or juice, often barrel-aged.

members.title: Vodka
members.description: Clear, neutral Eastern European drink from grain or potatoes.

members.title: Scotch whisky
members.description: Malted-barley drink aged at least three years in oak casks in Scotland.

members.title: Baijiu
members.description: Potent Chinese sorghum drink with a pungent, funky aroma.

members.title: Shochu
members.description: Japanese drink from sweet potato, barley, or rice, often served on ice.

members.title: Grappa
members.description: Italian drink from the grape skins and seeds left over from winemaking.

members.title: Cognac
members.description: French grape brandy aged in oak casks in the Charente region.

intruders.title: Sake
intruders.description: Japanese rice drink served warm or chilled from small ceramic cups.
intruders.why: Brewed and fermented but never distilled, at around 15 percent alcohol. Its cousin shochu is the distilled one.

intruders.title: Pulque
intruders.description: Milky, viscous Mexican drink from the sap of the maguey agave plant.
intruders.why: Agave sap that is only fermented. Tequila and mezcal come from agave too, but they are distilled.

theme: Breads made without any leavening: no yeast, sourdough starter, or chemical raising agent.
decoy: Flatbreads and traditional breads

members.title: Matzo
members.description: Thin, crisp, perforated cracker-like sheets eaten during Passover.

members.title: Chapati
members.description: Soft whole-wheat round cooked on a flat griddle in North Indian homes.

members.title: Corn tortilla
members.description: Thin disc of nixtamalized maize dough cooked on a comal.

members.title: Paratha
members.description: Flaky whole-wheat round folded with ghee and fried on a griddle.

members.title: Arepa
members.description: Thick round cornmeal cake from Venezuela and Colombia, split and stuffed.

members.title: Puri
members.description: Small whole-wheat round that balloons when fried in hot oil.

members.title: Hardtack
members.description: Rock-hard ship's biscuit of flour, water, and salt, stored for months.

members.title: Bhakri
members.description: Coarse, rustic millet or sorghum round cooked on a griddle in Maharashtra.

intruders.title: Naan
intruders.description: Pillowy teardrop-shaped round slapped onto the wall of a tandoor oven.
intruders.why: Its dough is leavened, usually with yeast, and left to rise before baking. It looks like the unleavened Indian flatbreads.

intruders.title: Pita
intruders.description: Round Middle Eastern pocket bread that puffs up hollow in a hot oven.
intruders.why: A yeast-raised dough: the pocket forms when steam inflates the risen dough. Puri also puffs, but without leavening.

intruders.title: Injera
intruders.description: Spongy, sour Ethiopian round of teff batter cooked on a large griddle.
intruders.why: The batter is fermented for days, and the wild yeast leavens it, making the bubbles on its surface.

theme: Dishes whose main ingredient is served raw, never cooked with heat.
decoy: Chilled or cold-served meat, fish, and vegetable dishes

members.title: Sashimi
members.description: Slices of fish arranged on a plate with wasabi and soy sauce.

members.title: Steak tartare
members.description: Minced beef mixed with capers and shallots, topped with an egg yolk.

members.title: Ceviche
members.description: Cubes of fish marinated in lime juice with red onion and chili.

members.title: Poke
members.description: Hawaiian cubes of tuna tossed with soy sauce, sesame oil, and onion.

members.title: Kibbeh nayyeh
members.description: Levantine paste of lamb and bulgur, drizzled with olive oil.

members.title: Yukhoe
members.description: Korean seasoned beef strips topped with egg yolk and slivers of pear.

members.title: Gazpacho
members.description: Chilled Andalusian soup of blended tomato, cucumber, pepper, and bread.

members.title: Mett
members.description: German minced pork seasoned with salt and pepper, spread on bread rolls.

members.title: Gravlax
members.description: Nordic salmon cured with salt, sugar, and dill, sliced thin.

intruders.title: Vitello tonnato
intruders.description: Thin slices of veal served cold under a creamy tuna and caper sauce.
intruders.why: The veal is roasted or poached first, then chilled and sliced. It looks like a raw-meat plate such as carpaccio.

intruders.title: Beef tataki
intruders.description: Japanese thin slices of beef, rare in the center, dressed with ponzu.
intruders.why: The beef is seared over high heat before slicing; only the center stays rare.

theme: Drinks that naturally contain caffeine from the plant they are brewed from.
decoy: Hot brewed drinks: teas, coffees, and infusions

members.title: Espresso
members.description: Small, concentrated shot pulled under pressure, topped with crema.

members.title: Matcha
members.description: Stone-ground powdered green tea whisked into a frothy bowl.

members.title: Yerba mate
members.description: South American infusion sipped through a metal straw from a gourd.

members.title: Oolong
members.description: Partly oxidized Chinese and Taiwanese tea with tightly rolled leaves.

members.title: Masala chai
members.description: Indian black tea simmered with milk, sugar, and warm spices.

members.title: Earl Grey
members.description: Black tea scented with oil of bergamot, often served with milk.

members.title: Pu-erh
members.description: Aged Yunnan tea pressed into cakes and bricks, earthy and dark.

members.title: Turkish coffee
members.description: Finely ground coffee simmered in a small pot and served unfiltered.

intruders.title: Rooibos
intruders.description: Red South African tea of needle-like leaves, often with milk.
intruders.why: Made from the Aspalathus linearis shrub, which has no caffeine. It is brewed and sold exactly like black tea.

intruders.title: Barley tea
intruders.description: Roasted-grain tea served iced in Japanese and Korean homes.
intruders.why: Roasted barley has no caffeine, though it is brewed and served as an everyday tea.

theme: Foods made from animal milk.
decoy: Rich, creamy, or buttery kitchen ingredients

members.title: Ghee
members.description: Nutty clarified butter used for frying spices and finishing dal.

members.title: Paneer
members.description: Firm, fresh, unsalted Indian cheese cubed into curries.

members.title: Creme fraiche
members.description: Thick, slightly sour French cream that won't split when boiled.

members.title: Skyr
members.description: Thick, high-protein Icelandic spoonable staple eaten with berries.

members.title: Labneh
members.description: Tangy strained yogurt spread drizzled with olive oil and za'atar.

members.title: Dulce de leche
members.description: Thick caramel spread beloved in Argentina and Uruguay, slowly cooked until brown.

members.title: Clotted cream
members.description: Thick English cream spread onto scones with strawberry jam.

members.title: Ricotta
members.description: Soft, moist Italian curd used in lasagna and cannoli.

members.title: Mascarpone
members.description: Rich Italian spreadable cream cheese folded into tiramisu.

intruders.title: Cream of tartar
intruders.description: Fine white powder used to stabilize whipped egg whites for meringue.
intruders.why: Potassium bitartrate, a by-product of winemaking. 'Cream' is in the name only.

intruders.title: Cocoa butter
intruders.description: Pale solid fat that melts at body heat, the base of white chocolate.
intruders.why: A fat pressed from cacao beans; 'butter' only describes its texture.

theme: Grains and pseudocereals that are naturally free of gluten.
decoy: Whole grains and ancient grains

members.title: Quinoa
members.description: Andean staple with tiny round kernels that uncurl little tails when cooked.

members.title: Buckwheat
members.description: Triangular kernels roasted into kasha and milled for soba and galettes.

members.title: Millet
members.description: Tiny yellow round kernels eaten as porridge across Africa and Asia.

members.title: Sorghum
members.description: Drought-hardy cereal popped like corn and brewed into African beers.

members.title: Teff
members.description: Minute Ethiopian cereal milled into flour for a spongy flatbread.

members.title: Amaranth
members.description: Tiny kernels once farmed by the Aztecs, popped and bound into bars.

members.title: Wild rice
members.description: Long, dark aquatic kernels harvested by canoe around the Great Lakes.

members.title: Fonio
members.description: Tiny, fast-cooking West African cereal steamed like couscous.

members.title: Maize
members.description: Staple cereal of the Americas, ground into masa, polenta, and grits.

intruders.title: Spelt
intruders.description: Hulled ancient cereal with a nutty flavor, popular in German baking.
intruders.why: A species of wheat (Triticum spelta), so it contains gluten. Its 'ancient grain' image groups it with quinoa and teff.

intruders.title: Farro
intruders.description: Chewy Italian ancient cereal simmered into salads and hearty soups.
intruders.why: Farro is hulled wheat (emmer, einkorn, or spelt), so it contains gluten.

theme: Cheeses made wholly or mainly from sheep's milk.
decoy: Famous protected-origin European cheeses

members.title: Roquefort
members.description: Crumbly, pungent blue cheese ripened in limestone caves in southern France.

members.title: Pecorino Romano
members.description: Hard, salty Italian grating cheese essential to cacio e pepe.

members.title: Manchego
members.description: Firm Spanish cheese from La Mancha with a zigzag-patterned rind.

members.title: Feta
members.description: White Greek cheese kept in brine and crumbled over salads.

members.title: Ossau-Iraty
members.description: Firm, nutty cheese from the French Basque Country and Bearn.

members.title: Idiazabal
members.description: Firm, often smoked Basque cheese with a buttery, nutty flavor.

members.title: Torta del Casar
members.description: Spanish cheese whose top is sliced off to scoop out the runny center.

members.title: Fiore Sardo
members.description: Hard, lightly smoked Sardinian cheese used for grating.

members.title: Zamorano
members.description: Hard Castilian cheese with a dark rind, aged for many months.

intruders.title: Gorgonzola
intruders.description: Creamy, blue-veined Italian cheese from Lombardy and Piedmont.
intruders.why: Made from cow's milk. It is the Italian counterpart people pair with Roquefort.

intruders.title: Parmigiano-Reggiano
intruders.description: Hard, granular Italian grating cheese aged in huge wheels.
intruders.why: Made from cow's milk, unlike Pecorino Romano, the grating cheese it is most often swapped with.

intruders.title: Mahon
intruders.description: Firm, tangy cheese from Menorca with an orange-rubbed rind.
intruders.why: A Spanish cheese made from cow's milk (only a small share of sheep's milk is allowed), unlike its neighbor Manchego.

theme: Fruits and nuts from plants of the rose family (Rosaceae).
decoy: Temperate orchard fruits, berries, and nuts

members.title: Pear
members.description: Sweet, grainy-fleshed orchard crop poached in wine or eaten ripe.

members.title: Quince
members.description: Hard, fragrant yellow orchard crop cooked into Spanish membrillo paste.

members.title: Apricot
members.description: Small velvety golden orchard crop, often dried or made into jam.

members.title: Sour cherry
members.description: Tart red orchard crop baked into pies and Black Forest cake.

members.title: Strawberry
members.description: Red berry studded with tiny specks on its skin, served with cream.

members.title: Raspberry
members.description: Soft, hollow red berry picked from thorny canes in summer.

members.title: Almond
members.description: Oval kernel eaten roasted, pressed into a drink, or ground into marzipan.

members.title: Loquat
members.description: Small orange orchard crop with large brown pits, common in China and Japan.

members.title: Medlar
members.description: Brown, apple-like crop eaten only after it softens and blets.

intruders.title: Blueberry
intruders.description: Small dusky-blue berry baked into muffins, pies, and pancakes.
intruders.why: In the heath family (Ericaceae), with cranberries and rhododendrons, not the rose family.

intruders.title: Fig
intruders.description: Soft, purple-skinned orchard crop with a jammy, speckled interior.
intruders.why: In the mulberry family (Moraceae), not the rose family, though it grows in the same orchards.

intruders.title: Black currant
intruders.description: Tart dark berry grown on bushes, cooked into cordials and jams.
intruders.why: In the gooseberry family (Grossulariaceae), not the rose family like raspberries.

theme: Pasta made by sealing a filling inside the dough before cooking.
decoy: Italian pasta shapes served with a stuffing

members.title: Ravioli
members.description: Square pillows stuffed with ricotta and spinach, served with butter and sage.

members.title: Tortellini
members.description: Small rings from Bologna stuffed with pork and mortadella, served in broth.

members.title: Agnolotti
members.description: Piedmontese pinched parcels stuffed with roast meats and greens.

members.title: Cappelletti
members.description: Hat-shaped Emilian parcels stuffed with cheese or meat, served in broth.

members.title: Mezzelune
members.description: Half-moons stuffed with cheese or vegetables, tossed in melted butter.

members.title: Culurgiones
members.description: Sardinian parcels of potato, pecorino, and mint with a braided seam.

members.title: Pansotti
members.description: Pot-bellied Ligurian triangles stuffed with wild greens, served with walnut sauce.

members.title: Caramelle
members.description: Candy-wrapper-shaped twists stuffed with ricotta or pumpkin.

members.title: Anolini
members.description: Small round Emilian parcels with a breadcrumb-and-parmesan stuffing, served in broth.

intruders.title: Cannelloni
intruders.description: Large tubes stuffed with ricotta and spinach, baked in tomato sauce.
intruders.why: Tubes (or cooked sheets rolled up) with open ends: the stuffing is piped in or rolled up, never sealed in.

intruders.title: Conchiglioni
intruders.description: Jumbo pasta shells stuffed with ricotta and baked under tomato sauce.
intruders.why: The shells are boiled first and then spooned full; they stay open and nothing is sealed.

theme: Sauces that are emulsions, getting their body from fat dispersed as tiny droplets rather than from starch.
decoy: Classic creamy sauces of French and Mediterranean cooking

members.title: Mayonnaise
members.description: Thick, pale sauce of egg yolk, oil, and lemon or vinegar.

members.title: Hollandaise
members.description: Warm, buttery yolk-based sauce spooned over eggs Benedict.

members.title: Bearnaise
members.description: Buttery yolk sauce flavored with tarragon and shallot, served with steak.

members.title: Toum
members.description: Fluffy white Lebanese garlic sauce served with grilled chicken.

members.title: Beurre blanc
members.description: Tangy Loire sauce of reduced white wine whisked with cold butter.

members.title: Vinaigrette
members.description: Tangy oil-and-vinegar dressing whisked with mustard for green salads.

members.title: Remoulade
members.description: Tangy mustardy sauce with capers and herbs, served with celeriac or fish.

members.title: Tartar sauce
members.description: Creamy white sauce with pickles and capers, served with fried fish.

intruders.title: Bechamel
intruders.description: Smooth white milk sauce, the base for lasagna and croque monsieur.
intruders.why: Thickened by a flour-and-butter roux, so its body comes from starch, not emulsified fat.

intruders.title: Veloute
intruders.description: Silky pale sauce made from white stock, served with chicken or fish.
intruders.why: Thickened by a roux, a starch-based mother sauce rather than an emulsion.

theme: Cocktails whose classic recipe uses gin as the base spirit.
decoy: Classic cocktails from the pre-Prohibition and cocktail-revival canon

members.title: Negroni
members.description: Bitter, ruby-red stirred drink with Campari and vermouth, garnished with orange.

members.title: Martini
members.description: Stirred, bone-dry drink with vermouth, served up with an olive or twist.

members.title: Tom Collins
members.description: Tall, fizzy sour with lemon, sugar, and soda over ice.

members.title: Gimlet
members.description: Sharp, pale sour shaken with lime cordial and served up.

members.title: Aviation
members.description: Pale violet sour with maraschino, lemon, and creme de violette.

members.title: Bee's Knees
members.description: Shaken sour sweetened with honey and brightened with lemon juice.

members.title: Last Word
members.description: Equal-measure shaken drink with green Chartreuse, maraschino, and lime.

members.title: Corpse Reviver No. 2
members.description: Shaken drink of Lillet, orange liqueur, lemon, and an absinthe rinse.

members.title: Bramble
members.description: Crushed-ice sour drizzled with blackberry liqueur, from 1980s London.

intruders.title: Americano
intruders.description: Bitter red drink of Campari and vermouth topped with soda, with orange.
intruders.why: Campari, sweet vermouth, and soda with no gin at all. It is the Negroni's ancestor.

intruders.title: Boulevardier
intruders.description: Bitter, ruby stirred drink with Campari and vermouth, with orange peel.
intruders.why: Made with bourbon or rye whiskey. It is the Negroni's whiskey twin.

intruders.title: Daiquiri
intruders.description: Sharp, pale sour shaken with lime juice and sugar, served in a coupe.
intruders.why: Made with rum. It mirrors the gimlet's lime-and-sugar build.

theme: Rice dishes traditionally made with short- or medium-grain rice.
decoy: Iconic rice dishes from around the world

members.title: Risotto
members.description: Northern Italian rice stirred with hot broth until creamy, finished with parmesan.

members.title: Nigiri
members.description: Hand-pressed ovals of vinegared rice topped with slices of fish.

members.title: Arancini
members.description: Sicilian fried balls of rice with ragu or cheese inside.

members.title: Onigiri
members.description: Japanese rice balls wrapped in nori around salted salmon or pickled plum.

members.title: Bibimbap
members.description: Korean bowl of rice topped with vegetables, beef, egg, and gochujang.

members.title: Arroz negro
members.description: Spanish rice cooked black with squid ink, served with aioli.

members.title: Suppli
members.description: Roman fried rice croquettes with a string of melted mozzarella inside.

members.title: Risi e bisi
members.description: Venetian spring rice with young peas, loose enough to eat with a spoon.

intruders.title: Hainanese chicken rice
intruders.description: Poached chicken on rice cooked in chicken fat and stock, with ginger.
intruders.why: Made with jasmine rice, a long-grain variety, toasted in chicken fat.

intruders.title: Jambalaya
intruders.description: Louisiana one-pot rice dish with sausage, chicken, and the holy trinity.
intruders.why: Made with long-grain rice.

intruders.title: Jollof rice
intruders.description: West African rice simmered in a spiced tomato and red pepper sauce, smoky.
intruders.why: Made with long-grain rice, often parboiled.

theme: Condiments whose heat comes from chili peppers.
decoy: Fiery, pungent condiments

members.title: Sriracha
members.description: Garlicky, slightly sweet red sauce named for a Thai coastal town.

members.title: Harissa
members.description: Fiery North African red paste with garlic, caraway, and olive oil.

members.title: Gochujang
members.description: Sticky, sweet Korean red paste of fermented soybeans and glutinous rice.

members.title: Sambal oelek
members.description: Coarse Indonesian red paste ground with a stone pestle.

members.title: Tabasco sauce
members.description: Thin, vinegary red sauce from Louisiana, sold in tiny bottles.

members.title: Zhoug
members.description: Sharp Yemeni green sauce blended with cilantro, garlic, and cardamom.

members.title: Nam phrik pao
members.description: Sweet, smoky Thai roasted paste with shallots and dried shrimp.

members.title: Shatta
members.description: Fiery Palestinian red paste of crushed fresh pods, salt, and olive oil.

intruders.title: Wasabi
intruders.description: Sharp green paste served with sushi that goes straight to the sinuses.
intruders.why: Its bite is allyl isothiocyanate from a brassica rhizome, not capsaicin from chili peppers.

intruders.title: Horseradish sauce
intruders.description: Creamy, sharp white sauce served with roast beef and smoked fish.
intruders.why: Its pungency comes from isothiocyanates in horseradish root, a brassica, not from chili peppers.

intruders.title: English mustard
intruders.description: Bright yellow, fiercely sharp paste served with ham and sausages.
intruders.why: Its heat comes from ground mustard seed (isothiocyanates), not from chili peppers.

theme: Cakes, breads, and sweets traditionally made for Christmas.
decoy: Festive European enriched breads, cakes, and confections

members.title: Stollen
members.description: Dense German loaf of dried fruit with a marzipan core, dusted in sugar.

members.title: Panettone
members.description: Tall, domed Milanese sweet bread studded with candied citrus and raisins.

members.title: Pandoro
members.description: Star-shaped golden Veronese sweet bread dusted with vanilla sugar.

members.title: Buche de Noel
members.description: French rolled sponge frosted with chocolate to look like a log.

members.title: Mince pie
members.description: Small British pastry tart of spiced dried fruit and suet.

members.title: Turron
members.description: Spanish nougat bar of honey, egg white, and toasted almonds.

members.title: Vanocka
members.description: Braided Czech sweet loaf with raisins and almonds, dusted with sugar.

members.title: Pan de jamon
members.description: Venezuelan bread rolled around ham, raisins, and olives.

members.title: Julekake
members.description: Norwegian cardamom sweet bread with candied peel and raisins.

intruders.title: Colomba
intruders.description: Dove-shaped Italian sweet bread with pearl sugar and almonds.
intruders.why: Made for Easter. It is Panettone's springtime sibling, from the same bakers and dough.

intruders.title: Kulich
intruders.description: Tall cylindrical Russian sweet bread with white icing and candied fruit.
intruders.why: The Orthodox Easter bread, blessed in church at Easter.

intruders.title: Simnel cake
intruders.description: British fruit cake with marzipan and eleven marzipan balls on top.
intruders.why: Made for Easter (and Mothering Sunday); the eleven balls stand for the apostles without Judas. It resembles a Christmas cake.

theme: Dishes traditionally cooked in an earth oven: a pit dug in the ground, heated with hot stones or coals, and covered over.
decoy: Whole-animal and communal feast-day roasts

members.title: Kalua pig
members.description: Hawaiian whole pig, smoky and shredded, served at luau feasts.

members.title: Hangi
members.description: Maori feast of meat, potatoes, and kumara wrapped and steamed for hours.

members.title: Cochinita pibil
members.description: Yucatan pork marinated in achiote and sour orange, wrapped in banana leaves.

members.title: Curanto
members.description: Chiloe feast of shellfish, meat, and potato dumplings under nalca leaves.

members.title: Lovo
members.description: Fijian feast of meat, fish, and taro wrapped in banana leaves.

members.title: Pachamanca
members.description: Andean feast of meats, potatoes, and fava beans layered with herbs.

members.title: Barbacoa
members.description: Mexican lamb or goat wrapped in maguey leaves and slow-cooked overnight.

members.title: Zarb
members.description: Bedouin feast of spiced lamb, chicken, and vegetables slow-cooked for hours.

members.title: New England clambake
members.description: Seaside feast of clams, lobster, and corn layered with seaweed.

intruders.title: Lechon
intruders.description: Filipino whole pig with crackling skin, the centerpiece of village fiestas.
intruders.why: Spit-roasted in the open over charcoal, not buried. It is the same kind of whole-pig feast as kalua pig.

intruders.title: Asado
intruders.description: Argentine feast of beef ribs, sausages, and offal, slow-cooked for hours.
intruders.why: Grilled on a parrilla or on iron crosses beside an open wood fire, not in a covered pit.

theme: Cooking techniques that use dry heat, with hot air, metal, flame, or fat as the medium rather than water or steam.
decoy: Core cooking techniques taught in culinary school

members.title: Roasting
members.description: Browning a joint or whole bird uncovered in the oven.

members.title: Grilling
members.description: Charring steaks on bars directly above a charcoal or gas fire.

members.title: Broiling
members.description: Browning the top of a dish under an intense overhead element.

members.title: Baking
members.description: Setting breads, cakes, and pastries in an enclosed oven.

members.title: Searing
members.description: Browning the surface of meat quickly in a smoking skillet.

members.title: Sauteing
members.description: Tossing small pieces briskly in a shallow skillet with a little butter.

members.title: Stir-frying
members.description: Tossing bite-sized pieces fast in a wok over a roaring burner.

members.title: Deep-frying
members.description: Submerging battered pieces in a vat of oil until golden and crisp.

members.title: Spit-roasting
members.description: Turning a whole animal slowly on a rotating rod beside a fire.

intruders.title: Pot roasting
intruders.description: Browning a tough joint, then leaving it covered in the oven.
intruders.why: Once browned, the joint sits covered with some liquid and cooks in moist heat: it is a braise despite the name.

intruders.title: En papillote
intruders.description: Sealing fish and herbs in a parchment parcel for the oven.
intruders.why: The food cooks in its own trapped steam; the oven only heats the parcel.

intruders.title: Braising
intruders.description: Browning meat, then leaving it lidded in a heavy dish for hours.
intruders.why: After browning, the meat cooks partly submerged in liquid: a moist-heat method.

theme: Dishes named after the pot, pan, or mold they are cooked in.
decoy: Hearty slow-cooked and oven-baked home-style dishes

members.title: Tagine
members.description: Moroccan slow-braised lamb or chicken with preserved lemon and olives.

members.title: Paella
members.description: Valencian saffron rice with rabbit, chicken, and beans, with a crisp base.

members.title: Cassoulet
members.description: Slow-baked Languedoc white beans with duck confit, sausage, and pork.

members.title: Casserole
members.description: Oven-baked layers of meat, starch, and sauce under a golden crust.

members.title: Terrine
members.description: Coarse pate of pressed meats, served cold in thick slices.

members.title: Tian
members.description: Provencal bake of thinly sliced vegetables in overlapping rows.

members.title: Potjiekos
members.description: South African stew layered over coals and left unstirred for hours.

members.title: Olla podrida
members.description: Spanish stew of beans, pork, and sausages simmered for hours.

intruders.title: Gratin
intruders.description: Oven-baked sliced potatoes or vegetables under a golden, crusty top.
intruders.why: Named for its crust (from gratter, to scrape). The gratin dish is named after the food, not the reverse.

intruders.title: Fondue
intruders.description: Swiss melted cheese and white wine, kept bubbling for dipping bread.
intruders.why: From fondre, 'to melt'. Its pot is called a caquelon.

intruders.title: Bouillabaisse
intruders.description: Provencal fish stew with saffron and rouille, with toasted bread.
intruders.why: Named for its method, from the Provencal for 'boil' and 'lower' (the heat), not for a vessel.

theme: Foods devised as stand-ins that imitate another, usually pricier or scarcer, food.
decoy: Foods with misleading or tongue-in-cheek names

members.title: Mock turtle soup
members.description: Victorian brown soup of calf's head, sherry, and forcemeat balls.

members.title: Mock apple pie
members.description: American pie of buttery crackers baked in a lemon-and-cinnamon syrup.

members.title: Crab sticks
members.description: Red-and-white sticks of surimi, a paste of white fish, for sushi rolls.

members.title: Margarine
members.description: Spread of vegetable oils churned into a yellow block or tub.

members.title: City chicken
members.description: Cubes of pork or veal threaded onto wooden skewers, breaded and baked.

members.title: Chicory coffee
members.description: Dark brew of roasted root served with beignets in New Orleans.

members.title: Lumpfish caviar
members.description: Tiny roe dyed black or red, sold in small jars for canapes.

members.title: Veggie burger
members.description: Patty of beans, grains, or soy, grilled and served in a bun.

intruders.title: Welsh rabbit
intruders.description: Toast under a sauce of cheese, ale, and mustard, grilled till bubbly.
intruders.why: A joke name for cheese on toast; it was never meant to imitate rabbit.

intruders.title: Bombay duck
intruders.description: Dried, salted fish from the Arabian Sea, fried crisp with curry.
intruders.why: A lizardfish eaten as itself; the name is a quirk and it imitates no duck.

intruders.title: Toad in the hole
intruders.description: Sausages baked in Yorkshire pudding batter with onion gravy.
intruders.why: A whimsical name for sausages in batter; it imitates nothing.

theme: Foods whose name, in its source language, simply names one or more of their main ingredients.
decoy: Foods known in English by a borrowed foreign name

members.title: Hummus
members.description: Levantine puree with tahini, lemon, and garlic, swirled with olive oil.

members.title: Tapenade
members.description: Provencal black spread of olives, anchovies, and capers for toast.

members.title: Aioli
members.description: Pungent Provencal garlic sauce pounded with olive oil.

members.title: Guacamole
members.description: Mexican mash of avocado, lime, onion, cilantro, and chile.

members.title: Sauerkraut
members.description: Finely shredded fermented cabbage served with sausages and pork knuckle.

members.title: Aloo gobi
members.description: Dry North Indian curry of potatoes and cauliflower with turmeric.

members.title: Palak paneer
members.description: Soft cheese cubes in a smooth, spiced spinach puree.

members.title: Arroz con pollo
members.description: Latin American one-pot meal of chicken and saffron-yellow rice.

intruders.title: Pesto
intruders.description: Genoese green sauce of basil, pine nuts, garlic, and parmesan.
intruders.why: From pestare, 'to pound': the name describes the method, not basil or any ingredient.

intruders.title: Tahini
intruders.description: Smooth, nutty Middle Eastern paste of toasted, hulled sesame.
intruders.why: From the Arabic root for 'to grind': the name describes the method, not sesame.

intruders.title: Ratatouille
intruders.description: Provencal summer stew of eggplant, zucchini, peppers, and tomato.
intruders.why: From French touiller, 'to stir': the name names no vegetable.

theme: Foods whose name is the same word said twice.
decoy: Foods with playful, sing-song names

members.title: Bonbon
members.description: Bite-sized chocolate or sugar confection wrapped in foil or paper.

members.title: Mahi-mahi
members.description: Firm, mild, sweet-fleshed ocean fish grilled for tacos.

members.title: Piri-piri
members.description: Tiny fiery African pepper behind Portuguese grilled chicken.

members.title: Gado-gado
members.description: Indonesian salad of blanched greens, tofu, and egg with peanut sauce.

members.title: Chow chow
members.description: Tangy relish of chopped green tomatoes, cabbage, and peppers.

members.title: Bang bang chicken
members.description: Sichuan cold shredded chicken dressed in a spicy sesame sauce.

members.title: Chin chin
members.description: Crunchy fried dough cubes, a favorite Nigerian snack.

members.title: Lomi-lomi salmon
members.description: Hawaiian side of salted salmon massaged with tomato and onion.

intruders.title: Tutti frutti
intruders.description: Colorful mix of chopped candied fruits folded into ice cream.
intruders.why: A rhyme, not a repeat: tutti and frutti are different words.

intruders.title: Hotchpotch
intruders.description: Hearty Scottish broth of lamb with summer peas, beans, and roots.
intruders.why: A rhyming compound (hotch and potch), not the same word twice.

intruders.title: Pani puri
intruders.description: Hollow crisp shells filled with spiced water, potato, and chickpeas.
intruders.why: Alliterative, but pani (water) and puri (the fried shell) are two different words.

theme: Foods whose standard recipe includes a non-obvious ingredient taken from animal flesh, fat, bones, or skin.
decoy: Sauces, sweets, and dishes that look plant-based at first glance

members.title: Worcestershire sauce
members.description: Thin, dark, tangy English sauce of vinegar, tamarind, and molasses.

members.title: Panna cotta
members.description: Wobbly Italian dessert of sweetened set cream with berry coulis.

members.title: Gummy bears
members.description: Chewy, translucent fruit-flavored candies shaped like little bears.

members.title: Marshmallows
members.description: Fluffy, spongy white candies toasted over campfires.

members.title: Pad thai
members.description: Stir-fried rice noodles with tamarind, peanuts, egg, and bean sprouts.

members.title: Refried beans
members.description: Mashed, twice-fried pinto beans served with Mexican breakfasts.

members.title: Tamales
members.description: Masa dough steamed in corn husks around a savory stuffing.

members.title: Thai green curry paste
members.description: Bright green paste of chilies, lemongrass, galangal, and garlic.

intruders.title: Turkish delight
intruders.description: Chewy cubes of rosewater jelly dusted in powdered sugar and starch.
intruders.why: Traditionally set with starch and sugar, not gelatin, unlike gummy candies.

intruders.title: Hoisin sauce
intruders.description: Thick, sweet, dark sauce brushed on Peking duck and char siu.
intruders.why: Made from fermented soybean paste. Its Cantonese name means 'seafood', but it contains none.

intruders.title: Cranberry sauce
intruders.description: Wobbly ruby jelly sliced from a can for Thanksgiving dinner.
intruders.why: Set by the natural pectin in cranberries, not by gelatin.

theme: Foods with a number in their name that literally counts their components or steps.
decoy: Foods with a number in their name

members.title: Tres leches cake
members.description: Sponge soaked in evaporated milk, condensed milk, and cream.

members.title: Quatre-quarts
members.description: Breton pound cake of equal weights of butter, sugar, flour, and eggs.

members.title: Three-cup chicken
members.description: Taiwanese favorite of chicken braised in sesame oil, rice wine, and soy.

members.title: Seven-layer dip
members.description: Party dip of beans, sour cream, guacamole, salsa, cheese, olives, and onion.

members.title: Quattro formaggi pizza
members.description: Pizza topped with mozzarella, gorgonzola, fontina, and parmesan.

members.title: Quatre epices
members.description: French spice blend of pepper, nutmeg, cloves, and ginger.

members.title: Twice-cooked pork
members.description: Sichuan pork belly boiled, sliced, then stir-fried with leeks.

members.title: Half-and-half
members.description: American carton mixing whole milk and light cream in equal measure.

intruders.title: Thousand Island dressing
intruders.description: Pink creamy dressing of mayonnaise, ketchup, and chopped pickles.
intruders.why: Named after the Thousand Islands region on the St. Lawrence River; it counts nothing in the dressing.

intruders.title: Century egg
intruders.description: Duck egg preserved in clay and ash until the white turns amber jelly.
intruders.why: Cured for weeks to a few months, not a hundred years.

intruders.title: Hundreds and thousands
intruders.description: Tiny colorful sugar balls scattered over fairy bread and cakes.
intruders.why: The numbers are figurative; they count nothing.

theme: Foods associated with a foreign cuisine that were actually first created in the United States.
decoy: Foods whose names or styles point to a foreign cuisine

members.title: Pepperoni
members.description: Spicy, paprika-red cured sausage sliced thin and crisped on pizza.

members.title: German chocolate cake
members.description: Layered chocolate cake spread with a gooey coconut-and-pecan frosting.

members.title: Crab Rangoon
members.description: Fried wonton wrappers around crab and cream cheese.

members.title: Cioppino
members.description: Tomato and wine stew of crab, clams, and fish, served with sourdough.

members.title: Russian dressing
members.description: Tangy pink dressing of mayonnaise, chili sauce, and horseradish.

members.title: French dip
members.description: Sliced roast beef on a baguette, dunked in meat juices.

members.title: Italian beef
members.description: Thin-sliced roast beef soaked in gravy on a roll with giardiniera.

members.title: Muffuletta
members.description: Round sesame loaf sandwich of salami, ham, provolone, and olive salad.

intruders.title: Fettuccine Alfredo
intruders.description: Ribbons of pasta tossed with butter and parmesan until creamy.
intruders.why: Created in Rome by restaurateur Alfredo di Lelio in the early 20th century. It is far more famous in America than in Italy.

intruders.title: General Tso's chicken
intruders.description: Crispy battered chicken in a sweet, spicy, glossy chili sauce.
intruders.why: Created in Taiwan by chef Peng Chang-kuei in the 1950s; American restaurants later made it sweeter.

intruders.title: Irish coffee
intruders.description: Hot coffee with whiskey and sugar, crowned with a layer of cream.
intruders.why: Created at Foynes in Ireland by chef Joe Sheridan in the 1940s; San Francisco only popularized it.

theme: Pastries made from laminated dough, where a slab of butter is folded into the dough again and again to create many thin layers.
decoy: Flaky, crisp European bakery pastries

members.title: Croissant
members.description: Crescent-shaped French breakfast roll with a honeycombed crumb.

members.title: Pain au chocolat
members.description: Rectangular French breakfast roll wrapped around two sticks of dark chocolate.

members.title: Kouign-amann
members.description: Breton round with a caramelized, sugary, crackling crust.

members.title: Mille-feuille
members.description: Stacked sheets of crisp pastry with pastry cream, iced on top.

members.title: Palmier
members.description: Heart-shaped cookie of sugared pastry rolled in from both sides.

members.title: Danish pastry
members.description: Sweet breakfast pastry with a fruit or cheese center and icing.

members.title: Vol-au-vent
members.description: Hollow, crisp pastry case spooned full of creamy chicken and mushrooms.

members.title: Pithivier
members.description: Domed, spiral-scored French pie around a core of almond cream.

members.title: Cronut
members.description: Ring-shaped fried pastry, cream-filled and glazed, created in New York.

intruders.title: Baklava
intruders.description: Syrup-soaked stack of crisp pastry sheets and chopped pistachios.
intruders.why: Made by stacking separate phyllo sheets brushed with butter one by one; the dough itself is never laminated.

intruders.title: Strudel
intruders.description: Paper-thin stretched dough rolled around apples and raisins.
intruders.why: The dough is stretched by hand and rolled up with fat brushed on, not laminated with butter folds.

intruders.title: Brioche
intruders.description: Rich, golden French breakfast bread made with eggs and butter.
intruders.why: An enriched dough with the butter kneaded straight in; there is no folding into layers.

theme: Sparkling wines whose appellation or legal category requires the traditional method: a second fermentation inside each bottle.
decoy: Prestigious European sparkling wines

members.title: Champagne
members.description: Northern French sparkling wine from Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, and Meunier.

members.title: Cava
members.description: Spanish sparkling wine largely from Penedes, often from Macabeo and Xarel-lo.

members.title: Franciacorta
members.description: Lombard sparkling wine from vineyards near Lake Iseo.

members.title: Cremant d'Alsace
members.description: Sparkling wine from Alsace, often based on Pinot Blanc.

members.title: Cremant de Loire
members.description: Sparkling wine from the Loire Valley, largely from Chenin Blanc.

members.title: Alta Langa
members.description: Piedmontese sparkling wine from Pinot Noir and Chardonnay grown in the hills.

members.title: Trentodoc
members.description: Sparkling wine from the mountain vineyards of Trentino, mostly Chardonnay.

members.title: Cap Classique
members.description: South African sparkling wine, much of it from Stellenbosch and Robertson.

intruders.title: Prosecco
intruders.description: Northeastern Italian sparkling wine from Glera grapes, light and fruity.
intruders.why: Prosecco's rules permit the tank (Charmat) method, and nearly all of it is made that way; a few producers bottle-ferment by choice, but the appellation does not require it.

intruders.title: Asti
intruders.description: Sweet, low-alcohol Piedmontese sparkling wine from Moscato Bianco grapes.
intruders.why: Made in pressurized tanks by a single fermentation that is stopped early to keep it sweet.

intruders.title: Sekt
intruders.description: German sparkling wine, a staple at weddings and New Year's Eve toasts.
intruders.why: German rules permit tank fermentation and most Sekt is made that way; bottle-fermented Sekt exists, but the category does not require it.
